season.locator: Ch. 3 (y5863e07.htm), 'Crop production systems': wheat is listed with the winter rotation
season.notes: Egypt-specific statement in an FAO country document. Month boundaries of the season are in seasons.yaml.

start_md.notes: Nile Delta wheat sowing window 10 Nov to 30 Nov as seen in a search-result snippet of the Global Yield Gap Atlas Egypt page; the page itself could not be opened (two attempts). Closest regional source (D2).

end_md.notes: See start_md. The same snippet gives physiological maturity between 15 Apr and 10 May for these sowing dates.

season_length_days.notes: Value from FAO-56 Table 11, row 'Grains (small)', 165 days, Oct/Nov, Pakistan; arid regions (no Egypt-specific row for wheat). min 136 and max 181 are computed (D5) from the sowing window (10-30 Nov) and the maturity window (15 Apr-10 May) in the unopened GYGA snippet: 30 Nov to 15 Apr = 136 days; 10 Nov to 10 May = 181 days. Locator (informational): Ch. 6, Table 11, row 'Grains (small)'

ini.notes: FAO-56 Table 11 row 'Grains (small)' (25/35/65/40 days), regional analog (D2). Other FAO wheat rows show wide variation (initial stage 15 to 40 days).

late.notes: Same row as ini. Stage days sum to 165 = season_length_days.

ini.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, group 'i. Cereals' (0.3); row 'Winter Wheat - with non-frozen soils' (0.7)
ini.notes: Default 0.30 (cereal group value). The 0.7 value for winter wheat on non-frozen soils is stored as max (D1: same source, conditions differ). Kc ini depends on wetting interval and ETo (FAO-56 Fig. 29/30, Annex 7); the planner should refine it from the irrigation interval. No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

mid.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Spring Wheat' (1.15); Box 14 (climate range 1.02 to 1.25)
mid.notes: Table default 1.15. Box 14 shows 1.02 (humid, calm) to 1.25 (arid, strong wind); for arid or semi-arid with moderate wind it gives 1.20. That climatic adjustment was not applied because local wind and humidity were not obtained.

end.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Spring Wheat' (Kc end 0.25-0.4) and footnote 10
end.notes: Lower value for machine harvest after full drying, higher value for hand harvest (footnote 10). Value is the rounded midpoint of the published range (a convenience; use min and max for sensitivity).

root_depth_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 22, row 'Spring Wheat' (1.0-1.5 m) and footnote 1
root_depth_m.notes: Value is the lower bound, which footnote 1 recommends for irrigation scheduling; the upper bound is for stress modeling or rainfed use. Winter wheat row is 1.5-1.8 m. Spring-habit wheat is assumed for Egypt (analyst judgment).

depletion_fraction_p.locator: Ch. 8, Table 22, row 'Spring Wheat' (p = 0.55) and footnote 2
depletion_fraction_p.notes: Valid for ETc about 5 mm per day; FAO-56 gives p = p(Table 22) + 0.04 (5 - ETc) and suggests lowering p by 5-10 percent on fine-textured soils. Neither adjustment was applied.

ky_total.locator: Table 1 (spring wheat 1.15; winter wheat 1.05) and Table 2, FAO column, total season (winter wheat 1.00; IAEA studies 0.87 and 1.32)
ky_total.notes: min and max span winter wheat in the IAEA comparison (0.87) to spring wheat in the IAEA comparison (1.32); FAO point values are 1.00-1.05 (winter) and 1.15 (spring). FAO-56 Table 24 gives 1.15 and 1.05 as well. Spring wheat row used as the central value (analyst judgment).

threshold_c.notes: Recalled from the wheat heat-stress literature: daily maximum air temperature near 30-32 degrees C around anthesis begins to reduce grain set; values up to about 35 degrees C are used for grain filling. Not read in an opened source.

sensitive_stage.notes: Recalled; consistent with the general statement in an opened FAO text that flowering and yield formation are the most water-sensitive periods, which is not a heat statement.

n_removal_kg_ha.notes: Order-of-magnitude removal in harvested grain for irrigated yields of roughly 6-7 t per ha at about 2 percent grain N; straw excluded. Recalled, not read in an opened source.

extra_water_mm.notes: Not applicable: only rice receives extra water beyond crop evapotranspiration. Fallback: the planner must use 0 mm.

threshold_ds_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 23, rows 'Wheat (Triticum aestivum)' 6.0, 'Wheat, semidwarf' 8.6, 'Wheat, durum' 5.7-5.9
threshold_ds_m.notes: ECe threshold in dS per m at 25 degrees C (saturation extract). Bread wheat 6.0; semidwarf bread wheat 8.6 (stored as max). Rating MT (moderately tolerant) to T.

slope_pct_per_ds_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 23, rows 'Wheat (Triticum aestivum)' 7.1 and 'Wheat, semidwarf' 3.0
slope_pct_per_ds_m.notes: Percent yield reduction per dS per m above the threshold. min 3.0 belongs to the semidwarf row (paired with threshold 8.6). Guideline values only (Table 23 footnote 1).

season.locator: Ch. 3 (y5863e07.htm), 'Crop production systems': berseem clover is listed with the winter rotation
season.notes: Egypt-specific statement in an FAO country document. The same chapter distinguishes long-season and short-season (catch) berseem; this entry parameterizes the long-season multi-cut crop.

start_md.notes: Analyst bracket of two observations: the unopened GYGA snippet lists berseem sowing 01 Sep to 31 Oct; the opened Egyptian trial (Zagazig J. Agric. Res. 2023, p. 151) sowed on 4 and 7 November. Start set to 1 October (D2, D4).

end_md.notes: See start_md; the opened trial sowed on 4 and 7 November, so the end is set to 15 November.

season_length_days.notes: Arithmetic from the opened trial (p. 151): cuts at 65 days, then 50, 40 and 30 days after the previous cut = 185 days after sowing (sown 4 and 7 November, four cuts, sandy loam, Sharkia). Single-site observation; range 150 to 240 days is an analyst bracket (the unopened GYGA snippet reports 5-7 cuts until April-June). Locator (informational): Materials and Methods, p. 151

ini.notes: Analyst allocation of the 185-day season to the four FAO stages; FAO-56 Table 11 has no berseem row. Range reflects that uncertainty.

mid.notes: Analyst allocation, see ini. FAO-56 uses one averaged mid-season period for hay crops (Table 12 footnote 13).

late.notes: Analyst allocation, see ini. Stage days sum to 185 = season_length_days.

ini.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Clover hay, Berseem' (averaged cutting effects 0.40; individual cutting periods 0.40)
ini.notes: Same value for both approaches. No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

mid.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Clover hay, Berseem' (averaged 0.90; individual cutting periods 1.15) and footnotes 13, 14
mid.notes: Default 0.90 is the average over cuttings (use with one season-long mid period); 1.15 is the full-cover value of a single cutting cycle (stored as max). No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

end.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Clover hay, Berseem' (averaged 0.85; individual cutting periods 1.10)
end.notes: Same logic as mid. No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

root_depth_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 22, row 'Clover hay, Berseem' (0.6-0.9 m) and footnote 1
root_depth_m.notes: Lower bound used for irrigation scheduling (footnote 1).

depletion_fraction_p.notes: Valid for ETc about 5 mm per day; no adjustment applied.

ky_total.notes: No berseem value exists in FAO Paper 33 as reproduced in the opened sources. FAO-56 (Ch. 8, 'Limitations') allows Ky = 1 or the value of a similar crop; alfalfa is 1.1 (Table 24). Alfalfa value used as an analog; min 1.0 is the FAO-56 default for unknown crops. Locator (informational): Ch. 8, Table 24 (Alfalfa 1.1) and 'Limitations' paragraph

threshold_c.notes: No defensible value found. Fallback: the planner applies no heat-stress penalty to berseem.

sensitive_stage.notes: No defensible value found. Fallback: no sensitive stage is assigned.

n_removal_kg_ha.notes: Gross N removed in cut forage if all cuts are removed from the field, from recalled forage dry-matter yields (about 8-12 t per ha) and N contents (about 2.5-3.5 percent). This is not a net balance: fixation is handled in rotation_rules.yaml.

extra_water_mm.notes: Not applicable: only rice receives extra water beyond crop evapotranspiration. Fallback: the planner must use 0 mm.

threshold_ds_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 23, row 'Clover, Berseem' (1.5; slope 5.7; rating MS)
threshold_ds_m.notes: ECe threshold in dS per m at 25 degrees C. Rating MS (moderately sensitive).

slope_pct_per_ds_m.notes: Percent yield reduction per dS per m above the threshold. Guideline value only.

ini.notes: FAO-56 Table 11 row 'Maize (grain)' 20/35/40/30 (June, Nigeria); regional analog (D2).

late.notes: Same row. Stage days sum to 125 = season_length_days.

ini.notes: Cereal group value; the Maize row itself has no separate Kc ini. No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

mid.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Maize, Field (grain)' (Kc mid 1.20; h = 2 m)
mid.notes: Taller crop, so climate adjustment matters more (Example 27 gives 1.30 for an arid, windy site). Adjustment not applied because local wind and humidity were not obtained.

sensitive_stage.notes: Recalled. An opened FAO text (Ky chapter) also shows flowering as the most water-sensitive period for maize, which is a water statement, not a heat statement.

season.locator: Ch. 3 (y5863e07.htm), 'Crop production systems': rice is listed with the summer rotation
season.notes: Egypt-specific statement in an FAO country document.

start_md.notes: Nile Delta rice sowing window 1 May to 15 Jun as seen in a search-result snippet of the unopened GYGA Egypt page; whether this is nursery sowing or direct seeding is not stated (D2).

season_length_days.notes: FAO-56 Table 11 row 'Rice' 30/30/60/30 = 150 days (Dec; May; Tropics; Mediterranean). Short-duration Egyptian varieties need about 120 days from planting to harvest according to an opened FAO country document (Ch. 3, 'Cropping patterns'), and the unopened GYGA snippet gives 110-140 days after sowing. Range 120 to 150 (D1, D2). Locator (informational): Ch. 6, Table 11, row 'Rice'

ini.notes: FAO-56 Table 11 row 'Rice' 30/30/60/30; regional analog (D2). Scale proportionally if a 120-day variety is modeled.

late.notes: Same row. Stage days sum to 150 = season_length_days.

ini.locator: Ch. 6, Table 12, row 'Rice' (Kc ini 1.05) and Table 14 (arid to semi-arid: 1.10 light wind, 1.15 moderate wind)
ini.notes: Table 12 default for sub-humid climate. Table 14 gives 1.10-1.15 for arid to semi-arid climates; the Table 14 adjustment was not applied because local wind class was not obtained. Range 1.05 to 1.15 recorded.

mid.notes: Standard-condition default. No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

end.notes: Published range; depends on drainage before harvest. Value is the rounded midpoint of the published range (a convenience; use min and max for sensitivity). No climatic or local adjustment was applied (standard-condition default).

root_depth_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 22, row 'Rice' (0.5-1.0 m) and footnote 1

depletion_fraction_p.notes: Footnote 4 defines this p as a fraction of saturation, so it is not directly comparable with p of upland crops. Flooded paddy is normally kept saturated.

ky_total.notes: Recalled: FAO Paper 33 total-season Ky for rice is close to 1.1. Rice is absent from Table 1 of the opened FAO-66 chapter and from FAO-56 Table 24, so the value could not be checked in an opened source. Range widened to what is known (D4).

threshold_c.notes: Recalled: daily maximum air temperature of about 33-36 degrees C at anthesis causes spikelet sterility. Not read in an opened source.

n_removal_kg_ha.notes: Removal in harvested grain for irrigated paddy yields of roughly 8-10 t per ha at about 1.1 percent grain N; straw excluded. Recalled, not read in an opened source.

extra_water_mm.notes: Water needed beyond crop evapotranspiration = soil saturation for puddling + water layer + percolation and seepage x flooded days. Inputs from two opened FAO manuals: SAT = 200 mm; WL = 100 mm; PERC = 2 mm per day (heavy clay) to 8 mm per day (sand), average 5-6 mm per day (the two manuals differ: heavy clay 2 vs 4 mm per day; D1). Computed (D5): min = 200 + 100 + 2 x 75 = 450 mm (heavy clay, short-duration crop, 75 flooded days); max = 200 + 100 + 6 x 105 = 930 mm (FAO average percolation, 150-day crop, 105 flooded days). Flooded days are an analyst assumption (season length minus 30-day nursery minus about 15 days of drainage before harvest). A single value would be false precision; if one is required, the arithmetic midpoint is 690 mm. Plausibility cross-check only: an opened FAO country document reports about 14,000 cubic meters per ha (1,400 mm) for short-duration varieties and 21,000-24,000 cubic meters per ha for older varieties as 'water consumption/evapotranspiration'; its basis is not stated. Locator (informational): fao_iwm_water_needs Ch. 4 Steps 4-6; fao_iwm_paddy_sched Ch. 4.4

threshold_ds_m.locator: Ch. 8, Table 23, row 'Rice' (3.0; slope 12.0; rating S) and footnote 6
threshold_ds_m.notes: ECe threshold in dS per m at 25 degrees C. Footnote 6: for paddy rice the values refer to the EC of the soil water while plants are submerged. Rating S (sensitive).

slope_pct_per_ds_m.notes: Percent yield reduction per dS per m above the threshold. Guideline value only.

seasons.description: Winter field-crop season (wheat, berseem). Month boundaries are an analyst convention built from the agricultural year (1 Nov to 31 Oct) and the winter/summer rotation described in an opened FAO country document; the exact month limits are not stated there (D2). The historical third 'nili' season is not modeled.
seasons.locator: Ch. 3, 'Crop production systems' and 'Cropping patterns' (agricultural year 1 November to 31 October)

seasons.description: Summer field-crop season (cotton, maize, rice). Cotton and maize may be sown in March or April, before the nominal start of this season; the sowing windows in crops.yaml govern. Month boundaries are an analyst convention (D2).
seasons.locator: Ch. 3, 'Crop production systems' and 'Cropping patterns' (agricultural year 1 November to 31 October)

effect.locator: Introduction, p. 149 (berseem fixes up to 33-66 kg N per ha for the following crops)
effect.notes: Range as stated in the opened article, which cites Williams et al. (1990) and Govindasamy et al. (2021) as the underlying sources; those were not opened. Wording is 'as much as', so 66 is an upper figure and 33 the lower figure of the quoted range. Not stated whether the credit applies to one following crop or is shared by several. Do not add a separate yield bonus on top of this credit for the same crop (double counting).

rotation_rules.notes: Legume nitrogen credit for berseem as a range. Mineral N recommendations for the following crop can be reduced by up to this amount.

effect.notes: Effect is the magnitude of the relative change in yield of the 'to' crop as a fraction (0.10 = 10 percent); direction gives the sign. Weak evidence, range only (D6). Direction recalled from Egyptian crop-sequence trials seen only as search snippets; magnitude is an analyst bracket.

rotation_rules.notes: Maize after berseem. Overlaps with the N credit; apply at most one of the two for nitrogen-related benefit.

effect.notes: Effect is the magnitude of the relative change in yield of the 'to' crop as a fraction (0.10 = 10 percent); direction gives the sign. Weak evidence, range only (D6). Direction recalled from an Egyptian rice-after-clover comparison seen only as a search snippet.

rotation_rules.notes: Rice after berseem. Overlaps with the N credit.

effect.notes: Effect is the magnitude of the relative change in yield of the 'to' crop as a fraction (0.10 = 10 percent); direction gives the sign. Weak evidence, range only (D6). Direction supported by an opened FAO country document, which lists berseem before cotton, ploughed in as green manure after one or two cuts, as a traditional fertility practice (Ch. 4); no magnitude is given there.

rotation_rules.notes: Cotton after berseem (short-season or ploughed-in berseem). Overlaps with the N credit.

assumptions.reason: No expert, farmer or agronomist reviewed any parameter in this package. All evidence grades were assigned by the author from the sources actually opened.
assumptions.planner_fallback: Present every value as a documented input from named sources, never as expert-reviewed or validated.
